step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Lower the Victim Body Temperature: While waiting for medical personnel to arrive, work to lower the victim's temperature (p. 28).

Step 4 - Immerse or Spray With Water: If possible, immerse or spray the person with cold water (p. 28).

quiz_item.question: When towing a water-skier or wakeboarder behind a motorboat, what crew roles, lifejacket gear, and boarding procedures are required for safety?
options: A. The boat driver watches the skier in a rear view mirror without a spotter, and the engine stays in neutral while the skier climbs the swim platform.
B. The skier wears an inflatable belt pack only if they cannot swim, and signals 'stop' by waving both arms up and down.

C. A dedicated observer must watch the skier and relay hand signals so the driver stays focused ahead, the skier must wear a USCG-approved PFD rated for water impact, and the engine must be shut off completely before anyone approaches the stern to board.
D. Two boats should tow the same skier side-by-side so one boat can block wakes from passing vessels.

Ring Buoys and Seat Cushions: Type IV throwables include ring buoys and seat cushions with straps (p. 17).
Never Substitute for Wearable Vests: They should never be used in place of a lifejacket (p. 17).
Hybrid Buoyancy and Inflation Design: Designed to have internal buoyancy and to inflate for additional flotation (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Never Substitute Throwable Devices: They should never be used in place of a lifejacket (p. 17).
Step 2 - Understand Hybrid Flotation Features: Designed to have internal buoyancy and to inflate for additional flotation (p. 17).
Step 3 - Respect Special Device Limitations: These flotation aids have special characteristics and limitations, and should not be used without specific training (p. 17).
Step 4 - Select Fitted Type III Vests: Most Type III ski vests are well-suited for water sports because they are comfortable and do not restrict movement (p. 17).

pamphlet_excerpts: Front Foot Weight for Stability: To keep the board from wobbling, puts lightly more weight on your front foot than on your back foot as the boat begins Alternate Method for Deep water (p. 59).
Partially Rotated Wakeboard Start Option: You may prefer to start out with the wake board partially rotated uptoward the front foot (p. 59).
Parallel Board Starting Position: Begin with the wake board out in front of you and parallel to the water's surface (p. 59).
Bent Knees and Straight Arms: Keep your knees bent and hold the rope handle with your arms straight (p. 59).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Position Board Parallel in Front: Begin with the wake board out in front of you and parallel to the water's surface (p. 59).
Step 2 - Bend Knees With Arms Straight: Keep your knees bent and hold the rope handle with your arms straight (p. 59).
Step 3 - Signal Driver to Accelerate Smoothly: When you are in position and ready, shout out "Hit it!" to let the driver know to accelerate (p. 59).

pamphlet_excerpts: Skill-Based Wakeboard Foot Angles: With wake boards, the angle of your feet on the board can be adjusted depending on your skill level (p. 17).
Finding a Comfortable Beginner Stance: As a beginner, you'll want to follow the steps below, fine-tuning the adjustments to find a stance that feels most comfortable (p. 17).
Shoulder-Width Binding Stance Spacing: Adjust the distance between the bindings to about shoulder-width apart, with your back foot slightly more toward the rear of the board for better (p. 17).
Back Foot Angle Alignment: Adjust the angle of the back foot so that it is straight across the board or turned outs lightly toward the back (at zero to 9 degrees) (p. 17).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Set Bindings Shoulder-Width Apart: Adjust the distance between the bindings to about shoulder-width apart, with your back foot slightly more toward the rear of the board for better (p. 17).
Step 2 - Align Back Binding Angle: Adjust the angle of the back foot so that it is straight across the board or turned outs lightly toward the back (at zero to 9 degrees) (p. 17).
Step 3 - Angle Front Binding Outward: Adjust the angle of the front foot so that it is slightly turned outtoward the front (9 to 27 degrees) (p. 17).
Step 4 - Test Binding Fit on Shore: Try the board on for size before you hit the water (p. 17).
